content: The document provides detailed guidance on certifying deaths during pregnancy, childbirth, or the postpartum period when COVID-19 is a confirmed or suspected cause of death. It was developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) in collaboration with its Classifications and Terminologies team, the Department of Data and Analytics, and the Department of Sexual and Reproductive Health and Research, including the HRP Special Programme. Financial support for this work was provided by USAID and the HRP Special Programme. The purpose of this guide is to assist healthcare professionals in accurately certifying deaths caused by COVID-19 in pregnant or postpartum women. It summarizes key points from international guidelines on death certification and classification, specifically tailored to this population. The guide should be used alongside the International Guidelines for Certification and Classification (Coding) of COVID-19 as a Cause of Death and the WHO Application of ICD-10 to deaths during pregnancy, childbirth, and the puerperium (ICD-MM). Key points for completing the International Form of the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death include the following: Causes of death should be recorded using the 2016 WHO International Form, which consists of two sections (Frame A and Frame B). Online training tools for cause-of-death certification are available. It is essential to complete the pregnancy status field (the pregnancy checkbox) to indicate whether pregnancy contributed to the death and, if applicable, the manner of death. For deaths due to COVID-19, the following points are emphasized: The term COVID-19 should always be used in death certification to avoid confusion with other coronaviruses. The death certificate should specify whether the virus was confirmed through laboratory testing or if it was a probable or suspected case. The underlying cause of death should be determined on a case-by-case basis, and the assignment of COVID-19 as a cause of death should not be based solely on the knowledge that the woman was pregnant and tested positive for SARS-CoV-2. For example, a woman with COVID-19 may have died from a direct obstetric cause, such as postpartum hemorrhage, or a non-obstetric cause, such as a car accident. When reporting deaths due to COVID-19, the term indirect should not be used to describe circumstances such as service disruptions caused by the pandemic. Indirect obstetric deaths are defined as those resulting from pre-existing or pregnancy-related conditions that were aggravated by the physiological effects of pregnancy. For instance, a death caused by pregnancy complicated by COVID-19 is considered an indirect obstetric death. Clear reporting is essential to avoid ambiguity about whether the data refer to excess maternal mortality during the pandemic or deaths where COVID-19 was a causal factor. The document also provides examples of how to correctly complete the International Form of the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death for various scenarios involving pregnant or postpartum women. These include cases of acute respiratory distress, bacterial pneumonia, severe hypoxia, and acute kidney injury, with detailed descriptions of the chain of events leading to death and contributing conditions. The WHO emphasizes that all reasonable precautions have been taken to verify the information in this publication. However, the responsibility for interpreting and using the material lies with the reader. WHO is not liable for any damages arising from its use. The document also includes references to additional resources, such as the WHO guidelines on ICD-10 and ICD-11, for further guidance on mortality coding and classification.
